biggest_catch: The $229 annual fee is the whole story, and the points have no fixed cash value: 60,000 Rapid Rewards points are worth roughly $750-$780 in Southwest flights at the program's typical value (about 1.25 cents per point), and you can only use them on Southwest. Year-one math: about $750 in flight value minus the $229 annual fee leaves roughly $521 net in the first year, before counting the card's $100 Southwest credit, upgraded boardings, and WiFi credits. Only claim this if you were already going to spend $2,000 in 3 months on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. Chase and Southwest's official restriction: the bonus is available only if you do not have a current Southwest personal card and have not received a personal Southwest cardmember bonus in the last 24 months (business cards are excluded).
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $2,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: 60,000 Rapid Rewards points are worth roughly $750-$780 in Southwest flights at typical program value, minus the $229 annual fee, which leaves about $521 net before travel perks. The $100 Southwest credit, upgraded boardings, and WiFi credits only have value if you actually fly Southwest and use them. Points are not cash and devaluation risk is real.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.

Chase and Southwest's official rule: this product is available to you only if you do not have a current Southwest Rapid Rewards personal credit card and have not received a new personal Southwest cardmember bonus within the last 24 months. This does not apply to Southwest business cards.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit.

Points post after the qualifying purchases and can take up to 30 days after your statement-cycle date to appear in your Rapid Rewards account; the account must be open and not in default when they post.

Confirm your eligibility: you do not currently hold a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card and have not received a personal Southwest cardmember bonus in the last 24 months.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $2,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow up to 30 days after the statement-cycle date for the 60,000 points to appear in your Rapid Rewards account.
Before the second $229 annual fee hits, audit which credits and perks you actually used and decide whether to keep, downgrade, or cancel based on real use.
